sources: issue #323, objective: 'every active faction move has a named leader responsible for carrying it out', four leader characters per faction, at most four leader-led active missions per turn
issue #323, data model (minimum): Leader, Faction, Relationship, Mission with leader_id REQUIRED, Event

issue #323, acceptance criteria: four leaders per faction; one active mission per leader per turn; members and resources amplify but never create free missions; one persistent portfolio with a bounded visible bonus; relationships and triggered choices change concrete strategy state
issue #323, non-goals: no separate CK3 court simulator, no global character network, no tactical combat or pathfinding, no full Terra Invicta council mechanics

provenance.source: issue #323 and its stage-A specification, plus the author-side design comment of 2026-10-13
provenance.note: the model is the author's directive and the design comment's; the schema is this session's

consumes.core: strategy_game/core.py already declares Leader and Faction containers; this layer extends them by addition and replaces nothing.
consumes.spec: strategy_game/docs/LEADER_COUNCIL_SYSTEM.md owns the written specification; this file implements its STRUCTURE and restates none of its prose.
consumes.quantities: the six quantities come from strategy_game/quantities.py, transcribed from docs/design/NOOPUNK_GLOBAL.md section 7.
consumes.edges: relationships are strategy_game.relationships.RelationshipEdge; the sparse record is not redeclared here.
consumes.leader_card: the Reason/Nerve/Rapport card in LEADER_MICRO_RULES_PROPOSAL.md is UNAPPROVED and is not assumed: a leader's attributes stay an uninterpreted author-defined mapping, so nothing below cares which attribute set is finally chosen.

council_size.source: issue #323's own acceptance criterion ('every player and rival faction has four leaders') and its own four-move cap ('at most four leader-led active missions per turn'); docs/LEADER_COUNCIL_SYSTEM.md section 1 records the fixed roster size as DRAFT.
council_size.not_this_question: This is ONE faction's leader roster. It is deliberately NOT the open question of which canonical faction records are canonical (the 4 / 7 / 11 data-integrity flag in docs/design/NOOPUNK_GLOBAL.md section 6A), which stays unresolved and is not touched here.

central_rule.rule: Every active faction move has exactly one named leader responsible for carrying it out. Members, volunteers, contacts, funds and equipment are resources and reachable capacity, never independent action slots.
structural_checks: a mission with an empty leader_id is invalid and is rejected
one leader cannot hold two active missions in the same turn
a faction cannot declare more active missions than it has leader-turns
declared resources amplify a leader-led mission and never add a mission
central_rule.source: issue #323 objective and acceptance criteria; stage-A specification section 1

portfolios.label: Politics & Diplomacy
portfolios.decides: the faction's posture toward incumbents, coalitions and courts: which doors are opened, which compromises are acceptable, and which institutional foothold is worth the price.
portfolios.argues_for: compromise, coalition, court the incumbent, bank a seat now

passive.reason: the stage-A specification proposes a bounded passive (at most +1, capped +2 faction-wide per turn) and marks every number DRAFT. A magnitude is a rule and no rule is approved, so this container records WHICH quantity the office touches and leaves the size to the author.

portfolios.label: Organisation & Networks
portfolios.decides: the base and the network: who is recruited, how the movement is organised, how far its reach actually extends, and whether that reach is owned or borrowed.
portfolios.standing_position: grow the base and the network
portfolios.argues_for: mass mobilisation, expand, refuse elite deals that hollow the movement

passive.reason: same as the office above: the quantity is named, the size is not approved.

portfolios.label: Operations & Resources
portfolios.decides: means and options: what is acquired, what is kept in reserve, what resilience the assets have, and how much of the faction's capacity is rented from someone else.
portfolios.argues_for: acquire, keep capability, take the ruthless option, protect the patron's money

passive.reason: same as above. Note that membership/resources appears in two portfolios' interests, which is not a collision: the quantity is one, the interests in it are two.

portfolios.label: Research & Intelligence
portfolios.decides: what is known and how it is framed: which claim is verified, which evidence is published, which signifier the faction makes nodal, and what it chooses to hold back.
portfolios.argues_for: investigate, verify, publish - or, on the other wing, publish first and apologise later
portfolios.quantity_note: Research and evidence are NOT one of the six quantities: evidence is not a track, it is what a claim is grounded in. This office reaches the six through institutional access (opening a door with knowledge) and through discursive hegemony (making an articulation nodal).

structural_disagreement.claim: The six quantities are non-identical by rule, and a faction is capped at four leader-led active moves per turn, so it CANNOT pursue all of its priorities in a turn. The council is therefore a scarcity mechanism, and scarcity is what turns four offices into four arguments. A council whose members always agree is a council whose four portfolios serve one quantity, which is precisely what the six-quantity rule forbids.
consequences: a faction can hold opinion/support and still lose seats (turnout, electoral rule)
a faction can win seats and not hold office (coalition arithmetic)
a faction can have a huge membership and no institutional access
a faction can hold the nodal signifier and lose everything else
structural_disagreement.reported_not_enforced: The code reports when the four portfolios' primary quantities are identical, when a quantity no office serves, and which quantities this turn's declared missions leave unpursued. It applies no consequence: what a covered or uncovered quantity is worth is a rule.
structural_disagreement.source: docs/design/NOOPUNK_GLOBAL.md section 7 and the #323 design comment, section 1

mission.leader_slot: one active mission per leader per turn; a leader spends the turn on one active mission or on hold/skip

authorisation.holder: the faction's principal, per the issue's own wording that the faction leader assigns strategy and chooses priorities
authorisation.open_question: whether the council can authorise a mission the principal has not, or refuse one the principal has ordered, is NOT decided here. The declaration records who authorised it and whether that is the principal is REPORTED, not enforced.

costs.label: one of the four leader-turns
costs.note: an opportunity cost measured in QUANTITIES NOT PURSUED, which is what the scarcity above means in practice

costs.label: the declared resources and assets
costs.note: named, never priced: the amounts are a rule and no rule is approved

costs.label: the leader may end the turn in a named status
costs.note: busy, injured or compromised. The status vocabulary is declared; which outcomes cause which status is stage-B work and is not implemented.

costs.label: drawing on a patron's asset stresses the patron edge
costs.note: issue #346 step 4: patron resources are not automatically faction property. A mission that names a patron edge is a dependence debt rather than a free resource, so the declaration records the edge instead of the funds.

failure_is_not_nothing.shape: a failed mission does not move the attempted quantity, and a DIFFERENT quantity moves the wrong way. A failure that moved nothing would be the empty-turn outcome the playtest checklist rules out.

examples.note: a failed negotiation can close the access it sought and cost legitimacy
a failed investigation publishes a CLAIM THAT IS NOT EVIDENCE; the evidence_model in data/global_factions.json is binding, and provenance stays UNKNOWN

failure_is_not_nothing.reason: which quantity a given failure moves, and by how much, is a rule. The shape is recorded so the container is not mistaken for the rule.

refusal.shape: a portfolio holder may contest or refuse a mission that cuts against their portfolio's quantity. A refusal is a STATE (decline, or the leader's own availability), not a scheduling accident, so the council's disagreement lands at the assignment step as a strategic fact rather than as table talk.
refusal.reason: whether a council refusal is a status or an authored choice is decision D6 in docs/LEADER_MICRO_RULES_PROPOSAL.md, unauthored. The slot is described; the rule is not made.

resolution.reason: no mission is resolved anywhere in this package. Gate A (leader RPG) and gate C (strategy) in docs/RULE_SYSTEM_RESEARCH.md are open, and AGENTS.md section 4 reserves resolution, thresholds and cadence to the author. The Mission record carries an uninterpreted outcome field that nothing here writes.

status_consequences.source: the status table in docs/LEADER_COUNCIL_SYSTEM.md section 4, every row marked DRAFT

rows.note: recovery timing is TODO: requires author specification
an unavailable leader never silently trades down into a lesser action; the slot is simply unused
exposure risk and the reduction are TODO: requires author specification

status_consequences.reason: every row is DRAFT, and three of the six carry a TODO. A mission led by a leader in a no-mission row is therefore REPORTED with the row cited, not refused: refusing it would implement an unapproved rule.

character_events.criterion: issue #323 acceptance criterion 6: 'Important NPC relationships and triggered RPG choices change concrete strategy state, not only dialogue'
character_events.data_model: issue #323's minimum data model lists Event: trigger, participants, choice options, state effects, short narrative text. This is that container and nothing else.
character_events.reason: Which events exist, which option is taken and what each option CHANGES are rules. Issue #323 stage E and the E1-E3 proposal are unapproved (docs/design/ISSUE_323_RULES_STAGES_BCDE_PROPOSAL.md), and strategy_game/RULEBOOK.md still says NO RULES APPROVED. The container declares the SHAPE so the decision is expressible; the deck's content and every effect's direction and size stay the author's.

trigger_kinds.label: a leader's status changed
trigger_kinds.observable_in: council.py LEADER_STATUSES, read on a CouncilLeader.status
trigger_kinds.note: issue #323 asks for triggers based on relationships and traits; this is the status vocabulary the layer already declares

trigger_kinds.label: a relationship edge changed state
trigger_kinds.note: the edge owns its state vocabulary; no second list of relationship states is declared here

trigger_kinds.label: a declared active move produced an outcome
trigger_kinds.note: nothing in this package writes an outcome, so nothing in this package can fire this trigger. The slot is declared; the mechanism is not

effect_target_kinds.label: a relationship edge's condition
effect_target_kinds.vocabulary: the edge's own declared state_vocabulary in relationships.py. Deliberately not a second list of states: the edge owns its vocabulary, so this container checks only that a target is named

effect_shape.note: an effect names WHAT it touches. declared is false on every effect here because how far it moves and in which direction is a rule.

options_rule.note: Issue #323's criterion 6 requires a triggered choice to change concrete strategy state and not dialogue alone, so an option that names no effect and gives no reason is refused by name. An option that names an effect whose size is unauthored carries declared false and its reason instead. The refusal is over the container's completeness, never over an effect.

tabletop_projection.primitive: strategy_game/tabletop/cards.py Card, with CardType.EVENT and CardRole.PLAYABLE_MOVE
tabletop_projection.note: the event container is a typed declaration that projects onto the ONE shared card primitive, exactly as faction_cards.to_card() projects its four card types. No second card type vocabulary is introduced.
tabletop_projection.prerequisites_and_effects: left empty on the primitive: what an option changes is gated work, so the projection carries labels and links only

options.label: carry the office until its holder returns

effects.reason: whether taking over an office exhausts a leader, and for how long, is a rule and no rule is approved
whether an unstaffed office costs opinion/support, and how much, is a rule and no rule is approved

events.note: ILLUSTRATIVE and placeholder: these leader ids are invented for the example, not canon, and no faction from data/global_factions.json is used. It mirrors the worked turn in docs/LEADER_COUNCIL_SYSTEM.md section 8 rather than asserting story content. narrative_text is EMPTY because the prose is the author's.

narrative_note.reason: issue #323 lists a short narrative text on the Event record and the placeholder's is empty: the writing is the author's, and no test reads it

strategic_channels.label: the tie gates whether a mission can be attempted, and what it costs
strategic_channels.note: a mentor or indebted edge to a target makes a negotiation a mission you can attempt; a suspicious edge makes the same mission illegal or costly
strategic_channels.reason: the correspondence between a tag and a mission's legality is a rule. It is transcribed here as declared data with enforced=false, so the layer reads the edge either way without granting anything.

strategic_channels.label: the tie is the conduit the quantities travel along
strategic_channels.note: a personal edge to another faction's leader IS the conduit for access, articulation and coalition (Castells). The RPG layer is therefore not extra: it is the graph on which four of the six quantities move.
strategic_channels.reason: which quantities travel along which tie is a rule.

strategic_channels.label: the tie decides whether a disagreement is a trade-off or a split
strategic_channels.note: two portfolio holders who disagree on strategy and share a rival opinion produce a leak or a quiet sabotage; two who disagree but are mentor or friend produce a compromise. The disagreement is resolved by the two structures that already exist - the portfolio's interest and the sparse relationship record - not by a die roll.
strategic_channels.reason: what a leak or a sabotage removes is a rule.

strategic_channels.label: the tie is written back as state at the end of the turn
strategic_channels.note: at step 7 of the turn order relationships update ALONGSIDE the six quantities, and the next turn's mission legality reads them: leader decision -> faction standing -> discourse -> who cooperates -> the next personal decision. One loop, not three mini-games.
strategic_channels.reason: the update rules are the turn engine, and no turn engine is approved.

worked_example.label: four moves against six quantities
worked_example.note: ILLUSTRATIVE and placeholder: these leader ids are invented for the example, not canon, and no faction from data/global_factions.json is used. The shape deliberately mirrors the worked turn in docs/LEADER_COUNCIL_SYSTEM.md section 8 rather than restating it, and shows the scarcity: four moves can name at most four of the six quantities.
worked_example.what_it_shows: Each move names WHICH of the six it tries to move, which is what stops a mission being a generic success roll: winning the ward (legislative representation) and winning the crowd (opinion/support) are different missions, not one mission with different modifiers. Four leaders, four moves, and two priorities nobody at the table is pursuing this turn - the argument the council is having, in one table.

cautions.note: rival and player factions obey the SAME constraint: the validator takes any number of councils and applies no special case, so a rival cannot bank unused missions or gain free actions from members.
no separate CK3 court simulator, no global character network, no tactical combat or pathfinding, no full Terra Invicta council mechanics. Members stay abstract.
the six quantities are orientations and standing; demands, antagonisms and nodal signifiers drive actual articulation. Covering a quantity is not winning a hegemony.
reach depends on concrete networks and access, which is why a personal tie is modelled as a channel rather than as a bonus.
four leaders, four offices, sparse ties. No dense all-to-all graph and no per-member simulation.
